title: Schiller Cafe to Reisenweber's: the New York sensation
summary: The band gets the name Original Dixieland Jazz Band, goes to New York in January 1917 and becomes a hit at the 400 Room.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Over the Shilly cafe was made June. I mean March April and May And in June We work at the lab it could be in July It worked there to the last last part of December with shields This is the band that got the name original Dixieland jazz band Because prior to that we had no building We were building at this place as the original Dixieland jazz band by Harry James Cards were given out there may have been notices in the paper. I don't know now They had many musicians who went and played at this place that we left at the Shiller all of them to fail None of made a success the crowd followed us And it was here that Jolson and all the theatrical people would come in to hear this music Jolson induced max hot then a theatrical agent to take us to New York for a tryout Two weeks tryout we spoke it over amongst the boys And we all agreed what we got to lose we may stay all our life We ain't gonna get no further unless you make it the Broadway and make a hit you ain't nobody So we take the chance We arrived in New York around January the 7th we had no tuxedas no photographs The agent put the money off for us to come up there And we laid around New York for about eight days Getting photographs made Having tuxedas fitted to us And then we were ready to open it rise my whistle And it was a new room that opened on the 15th i'm not sure whether it's the right day on the 17th But we had already played at the paradise room for sample you know what I mean And we played at the coconut roof to see how the music would go When we opened up the 400 room The people got in there and they'd be on their plates they did everything they could we opened up with the tiger rack Well, they've been used to hearing violins and other soft instruments and we blasted it out It was a big crowd in there So some of them began take them farmers back home and send them back where they belong Our agent happened to be there He asked Mr. Schultz to get up and make an announcement Mr. Schultz happened to know a couple of young couples there He said get up and try to dance to the music He says you know this music is not for listeners it's for dancing So they got up and danced the first one couple and two couples and the whole thing was crowded That night that morning we didn't get off the five o'clock From then on we were a sensation And we crowded a place every night weekdays as well as uh Saturdays Sundays was no different All the great actors come there, Carlisle Blackwell Charlie Chaplin The J. Drew Franklin signs Remember the United States Treasury used to bring in 20 dollar brand new bills off the press And we used to collect a nice sugar can as high as 100, 150 to 200 dollars per night We went there for about uh It was 700 dollars I believe or 750 And after the four weeks was up we got 1200 dollars a week Now for five men getting 1200 dollars a week And having all these bullfrogs crowing down here about jazz They must have been either attending to their knitting Or they didn't have the stuff It ain't that they didn't try because they came Like I told you before March of 6 came the Creole Band Red Brown reorganized his band he came Johnny Fisher came the Detroit boys came And all of them went back to no means With the tail between the legs and the ears hanging down
